en.title: RAS inhibitor dosing: from public PK/PD data to target-coverage scenarios
en.summary: Public blood–tumor–DUSP6 reconstruction and hypothetical QD/BID comparisons with target turnover, variability and exposure costs.
key_findings: A public mouse blood–tumor–DUSP6 model was reconstructed and used to compare explicitly hypothetical QD, BID and TID regimens at the same normalized daily amount.

In a reference virtual population, splitting the same daily amount raised the proportion keeping a concentration threshold for at least 90% of the interval from 20.6% to 61.5%; these are simulations, not response rates.

Plasma half-life alone does not set dosing frequency: distribution, potency, target turnover and the lower tail of exposure decide where splitting matters, and these must be measured for a new RAS inhibitor.
